perstate v1.1.0: performance optimization & content index
> github: https://github.com/graphwisdom/perstate

Performance release for large knowledge graphs (100k entities: from unusable grep to seconds-scale).

Performance (pure shell + git + awk, no third-party deps):
- Content index (perstate-index.sh): concatenates all file contents into a single stream; search/info scan the index via awk instead of per-file grep -r. 100k entities / 300k relations: search ~120s -> ~5s (24x)
- Index auto-refresh: search/info rebuild the index automatically when absent or HEAD-mismatched; users never maintain it manually
- Sync cache (~/.perstate/.sync/): within window (60s write / 300s read) skips redundant git fetch+pull; a save immediately followed by search makes zero network round trips
- Redundant fetch elimination: pull fetches internally; the standalone fetch before it was removed
- Conditional worktree prune: runs only when worktree is missing/invalid, not on every call
- awk-batch extraction: view.sh/info.sh use single-pass awk instead of per-file grep/sed/cat forks; 2207-entity graph 2m42s -> 2.9s (56x)
- Fast search script: grep -RErIn batch scan, --read mode, reverse lookup, N-hop traversal
- O(n) statistics: valid/superseded counts via single awk scan (FNR==1 boundary detection, BSD-compatible) replacing O(n^2) nested grep

perstate v1.0.0 — Initial release

- Introduces a git-native remote knowledge graph for persistent agent and user state.
- Supports commands for memory status, saving insights, searching, forking branches, switching, stats, visualization, and cleanup using `/perstate`.
- Features auto-extraction, deduplication/merging, multi-hop queries, and graph visualization.
- Structured initialization and session binding flows ensure per-session branch management in multi-repo architecture.
- Stores knowledge as entities and relations in a file-based graph standard, versioned via Git.
